title: Daily Debrief — Thursday Nov 12, 2026
html:
Nvidia's CEO walked out, and SPY slipped back onto its 50% line.

Here's what I'm seeing. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO, oil jumped on Iran headlines, and the 10-year yield pushed toward 5%. SPY lost only 0.4%, but travel took the hit, and two of your levels did exactly their job: XOM finally closed over your 2.0 extension, and Nvidia's collapse stopped right at your 0.5.

The one thing

SPY closed $757.12, five cents under its 50% line at $757.17. Above $765 the $780 call triggers. A close under $751.39 says the bounce is over.

Nvidia said co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and director, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO; earnings stay on Tue Nov 17. The stock opened at $151, touched $148.80, and fought back to close $166.19 (−4.3%). Rivals rose: AMD +5.9%, Broadcom +5.5%.

Crude rose about 2.6% to ~$88.75 after President Trump said the U.S. no longer needs a deal with Iran. That lifted XOM (+1.8%) and OXY (+2.0%) and sank travel: DAL −5.2%, CCL −4.4%, RCL −3.9%.

SPY slipped 0.4% to $757.12 (S&P 500 7,592), the Nasdaq −0.4%, small caps (IWM) −1.6%. The 10-year yield rose toward 5% (reports range from 4.98% to 5.10%) and the VIX fear gauge rose 7% to 18.7. October producer prices (PPI) come Friday at 8:30 a.m.

The market in one picture — SPY

  • $781.62 — Oct 6 record high · target 2
  • $771.15 — 78.6% of the drop · target 1
  • $763–765 — Ceiling · 61.8% + 50-day · trigger
  • $757.17 — 50% line · closed 5¢ under
  • NOW $757.12
  • $751.39 — 38.2% · stop line for the call
  • $744–745 — Confluence · 23.6% of drop + big run
  • $729–733 — 200-day + Nov 5 low

How I read it: the high, $763.04, poked 10 cents through the 61.8% line of the Oct 6 → Nov 5 drop ($762.94) and got sold, with the 50-day average ($764.43) right above. That's two days in a row the $763–765 ceiling has turned SPY away. The close sat on the 50% line, $757.17. A close over $765 opens $771.15; a close under $751.39 sends SPY back to the $744–745 confluence.

Your names that matter today

Why these names: DAL and PLTR carry open calls and both slipped back under a level today, Nvidia had the day's biggest story and bounced off your own 0.5 extension, and XOM made its first close over your 2.0 extension since Nov 5.

DAL $86.55 · −5.2% — Wait · $90 call holding

  • What happened: Down 5.2% to $86.55, the low of the day ($86.41) right at the close. Oil jumped on the Iran headlines, and fuel is an airline's second-biggest cost.
  • The chart: It lost the 23.6% pullback line of the Oct 20 → Nov 10 run ($88.18) and closed just above the 38.2% at $85.50. The trend is still up (50-day $81.64 over the 200-day $77.20) and RSI is 55, not broken. The $83 stop sits on the 50% line, $3.55 below.
  • Watching: The $90 call is marked $280.50 (−$352 on paper, bid/ask $2.74/$2.87). Stop: DAL below $83. A close back over $88.18 would put the run back on track; target 2 is $95.18. No adding to a loser.

  • What happened: Dipped to $168.25, then closed $171.58, 65 cents back under the $172.23 trigger. It held above Wednesday's low ($170.80) on the close, so the early-warning line is intact.
  • The chart: Uptrend (50-day $185.08 over the 200-day $153.64), RSI 42. It's chopping right on the 38.2% line of the Jun–Oct run. Not a failure yet: the plan's exit is a close under $158, under the 50% line.
  • Watching: The $180 call is marked $705 (−$52.50, bid/ask $6.95/$7.15). Targets $182.77, then $185.5–190. A close over $172.23 again is the first good sign; a close under $168.25 would say the bounce is fading.

NVDA $166.19 · −4.3% — Avoid till earnings

  • What happened: Huang's resignation hit before the open. Nvidia opened at $151.01, bottomed at $148.80, and closed $166.19: a 12% climb off the low. Volume was 737 million shares, about double Wednesday's.
  • The chart: The low pierced your 0.5 extension at $155.33 and my 2.0 down-extension at $153.61, then closed $10.86 back above both: a wick, not a break. The close sat on the 1.618 down-extension ($166.29), under your 0.786 ($170.22). RSI 26, deeply oversold.
  • Watching: Earnings Tue Nov 17 sit inside every contract, and options are pricey: the Dec $155 put is IV 60% vs moves 44% → EXPENSIVE (1.36). Watch only. A close over $170.22 (your 0.786) is the first repair; a close under $153.61 means the wick failed.

  • What happened: Opened at $168.25 and never went back under your 2.0 extension at $166.89 (low $167.34). Closed $169.78, the first close over that line since it broke on Nov 5, after four failed tries (highs $166.79, $165.55, $164.96, $166.75).
  • The chart: An old ceiling just turned into a floor. It also closed back over the 50-day ($169.21), with the uptrend intact (200-day $155.12) and RSI 47, so it isn't stretched. Your next level up is the 2.382 at $174.69, then the 2.618 at $179.51.
  • Watching: A move over today's high, $171.00, is the trigger for the Dec $170 call. Out on a close under $166.50, just below your 2.0. Targets $174.69, then $179.51. One risk: an Iran deal headline could knock oil back fast.

Quick notes

  • HLT $372.73 · −1.1%. The $380 call is marked $870 (+$110 on paper), but its quote is very wide tonight ($6.70/$10.70, 51 traded). If you sell, use a limit near the mid. Exit on a close below $359.41; target 1 $385.93.
  • BA $171.55 · −1.7%. Still in its $165–179 box, 4% above the $165 put trigger. The Dec $170 put's spread is back inside the rule ($5.50/$5.90, 7%), IV 32% vs moves 36% → CHEAP. Not triggered.

Lesson of the day: Judge the trade by the stock, not by the option's red number

Your DAL $90 call lost 44% today ($5.05 to $2.81) while DAL itself fell 5.2%. That's leverage working in reverse. An option moves several times faster than the stock, so the option's P/L will always look scarier than the chart.

DAL today: −5.2% ($91.32 → $86.55) · The $90 call: −44% ($505 → $280.50)

The plan never said "sell if the call is down 50%." It said sell if DAL breaks $83, the 50% line of its run. DAL is $3.55 above that. So the question tonight is not "how much am I down?" but "is the reason I bought still true?" The uptrend is intact and the stop hasn't been touched. Two honest caveats: time is now working against the call (it loses about $5.60 a day to time decay), and the most you can still lose is the $280.50 that's left. That's why we size every play so that losing all of it doesn't hurt the account.

Plays on deck (Options Playbook)

PLTR Dec 18 $180 call (open since Nov 11) — $705 now · entry $757.50 · most you can lose

Why: uptrend plus RSI under 40 (your tested edge), chopping on the 38.2% line. Entry: $757.50 intraday Nov 11. Exit: a close below $158. Targets: $182.77, then $185.5–190.

OI 8,527 · vol 684 · bid/ask $6.95/$7.15 (2.8% spread) · delta 0.41 · IV 47% vs moves 50% → FAIR (0.94) · no earnings inside

SPY Dec 18 $780 call (watching) — $451.50 · most you can lose

Why: a breakout over the $763–765 ceiling (61.8% + 50-day) would aim at the old high. Enter: SPY above $765.00. Exit: SPY below $751.39. Targets: $771.15, then $781.62.

OI 38,270 · vol 2,782 · bid/ask $4.49/$4.54 (1% spread) · delta 0.27 · IV 12% vs moves 15% → CHEAP (0.82) · no earnings inside

XOM Dec 18 $170 call (new) — $567.50 · most you can lose

Why: your 2.0 extension flipped from ceiling to floor today, with oil the strongest theme. Enter: XOM above $171.00. Exit: a close below $166.50. Targets: your 2.382 $174.69, then 2.618 $179.51.

OI 9,982 · vol 1,437 · bid/ask $5.60/$5.75 (2.6% spread) · delta 0.51 · IV 28% vs moves 27% → FAIR (1.06) · no earnings inside (XOM reports late Jan)

Skip this: Nvidia anything before Tuesday's report: puts and calls are EXPENSIVE (IV/moves 1.31–1.36) and the premium drains after earnings. Buying the travel dip (DAL, CCL, RCL) while oil is spiking. A second DAL call while the first one is underwater. AMD's +5.9% pop: its nearest calls cost over $1,200.

Scorecard: 2 closed, 2-0, +$806.50 · 3 open (paper −$294.50) · 3 watching · early read

Homework

  1. On XOM, watch tomorrow's low against your 2.0 at $166.89. A true flip from ceiling to floor holds on the retest. A close back under it would make today a fake-out.
  2. On DAL, mark $85.50 (38.2%) and $83.00 (the stop). Note where tomorrow's low lands between them, and whether buyers show up at $85.50.

DAL's call is down 56% from entry, but DAL is still $3.55 above the stop. Is there any reason you'd sell before $83? Write the rule down before the open.

Set these alerts

  • DAL — price crosses below $83.00 → stop on the $90 call
  • PLTR — price crosses below $160.00 → near the $158 close-exit line
  • SPY — price crosses above $765.00 → call trigger for the $780 call
  • XOM — price crosses above $171.00 → call trigger for the $170 call
  • BA — price crosses below $165.00 → put trigger (check the spread)

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Fib in action · Wick or break? (Fibonacci Playbook)

Nvidia stabbed through two Fib levels and closed back above them

A level only "breaks" when price closes through it. An intraday stab that closes back on the other side is a wick: sellers pushed, buyers pushed harder. Today Nvidia gave us the cleanest example of the year.

The levels: your 0.5 extension, $129.31 + 0.5 × $52.05 = $155.33. My downside extension of the October slide (A Oct 6 $243.37, B Oct 23 $210.18, C Oct 28 $219.99, A − B = $33.19): 2.0 = 219.99 − 33.19 × 2 = $153.61. Two ladders, drawn differently, landing $1.72 apart: that's a cluster.

  • $243.37 — A · Oct 6 high
  • $219.99 — C · Oct 28 bounce
  • $210.18 — B · Oct 23 low
  • $174.12 — 1.382 down-ext
  • NOW $166.19
  • $153.6–155.3 — 2.0 down-ext + your 0.5 · WICK
  • $148.80 — Today's low
  • $140.93 — 2.382 down-ext
  • $133.10 — 2.618 down-ext

What price did: opened $151.01, low $148.80 ($6.53 under your 0.5), close $166.19, $10.86 above it. Both levels = WICK. Last night's try-it answers: 2.382 = 219.99 − 79.06 = $140.93, 2.618 = $133.10; the low stopped $7.87 above the 2.382. For a trade: a put holder takes profit in a cluster like this. A bounce buyer would put the stop just under today's low ($148.80) and target $170.22, then $174.12. But Tuesday's earnings and EXPENSIVE options make it watch-only.

Try it: what's the 50% retracement of today's NVDA range, low $148.80 to high $167.14? (Answer Friday.)

Nvidia's CEO walked out, and SPY slipped back onto its 50% line.

Here's what I'm seeing. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO, oil jumped on Iran headlines, and the 10-year yield pushed toward 5%. SPY lost only 0.4%, but travel took the hit, and two of your levels did exactly their job: XOM finally closed over your 2.0 extension, and Nvidia's collapse stopped right at your 0.5.

The one thing

SPY closed $757.12, five cents under its 50% line at $757.17. Above $765 the $780 call triggers. A close under $751.39 says the bounce is over.

Nvidia said co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and director, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO; earnings stay on Tue Nov 17. The stock opened at $151, touched $148.80, and fought back to close $166.19 (−4.3%). Rivals rose: AMD +5.9%, Broadcom +5.5%.

Lesson of the day

Judge the trade by the stock, not by the option's red number

Your DAL $90 call lost 44% today ($5.05 to $2.81) while DAL itself fell 5.2%. That's leverage working in reverse. An option moves several times faster than the stock, so the option's P/L will always look scarier than the chart.

Fib in action · Wick or break?

Nvidia stabbed through two Fib levels and closed back above them

A level only "breaks" when price closes through it. An intraday stab that closes back on the other side is a wick: sellers pushed, buyers pushed harder. Today Nvidia gave us the cleanest example of the year.

The levels: your 0.5 extension, $129.31 + 0.5 × $52.05 = $155.33. My downside extension of the October slide (A Oct 6 $243.37, B Oct 23 $210.18, C Oct 28 $219.99, A − B = $33.19): 2.0 = 219.99 − 33.19 × 2 = $153.61. Two ladders, drawn differently, landing $1.72 apart: that's a cluster.

What price did: opened $151.01, low $148.80 ($6.53 under your 0.5), close $166.19, $10.86 above it. Both levels = WICK. Last night's try-it answers: 2.382 = 219.99 − 79.06 = $140.93, 2.618 = $133.10; the low stopped $7.87 above the 2.382. For a trade: a put holder takes profit in a cluster like this.
